statement: For every type P ∈ {r, +, −}, initialize the nearest-neighbor model as in Section 6. As long as the input couplings lie in their admitted bands, the exact observations produce representations with all renewed shape caps and the recursion bj−1 = bj + αP N−j + κP N−j bj + ∆j, |∆j| ≤ CLH−1.05 j . (12.4) There are CL < ∞, 0 < σ1 < 1, and a number κ∞ such that |αP h + γ| + |κP h − κ∞| ≤ CLσh 1 (h ≥ 0). (12.5) 96 These sequences are independent of the precise running couplings, and remain fixed when H is increased. The two inclined types have the same scalar sequences. On common ordinary steps, with discrepancy variables defined above, uj−1 ≤ quj + CL poly(Hj)ϵh + ej|λj|, |λj−1 − λj| ≤ CLuj + CL poly(Hj)ϵh + ej|λj|, ej = CL(log Hj)C /Hj. (12.6) If the histories share their last m ordinary observations, ϵh may be taken to be rm 0 , where r0 = A0/L2. The choices can be made with max{q, r0} < ρ < L−2+υ < 1 (12.7) and strict spare width. Here q and ρ are fixed bounds valid for every subsequent sufficiently large H. The corresponding free kernels and their lifts compare in the exponential kernel norms of Proposition 4.3 with the same history bound.
